cases.name: 01-tangent-external
cases.note: circles meet at the single point (1, 0)

cases.name: 02-tangent-internal
cases.note: smaller circle touches the inside of the larger at (1, 0)

cases.name: 03-vertex-on-vertex
cases.note: squares share exactly the corner (1, 1)

cases.name: 04-vertex-on-edge
cases.note: rotated square touches the middle of A's right edge with a vertex

cases.name: 05-edge-shared-full
cases.note: collinear overlap along the whole of the edge x = 1

cases.name: 06-edge-shared-partial
cases.note: collinear overlap along half of the edge x = 1

cases.name: 07-edge-shared-inside
cases.note: B's whole left edge lies strictly inside A's right edge

cases.name: 08-arc-shared-partial
cases.note: B shares 60 degrees of A's rim: a coincident stretch that is curved, and whose ends fall inside A's quarter arcs rather than on its vertices

cases.name: 09-arc-shared-full
cases.note: B's inner ring is the whole of A's boundary traced backwards

cases.name: 10-circle-tangent-to-edge
cases.note: curve meets line tangentially, where 01/02 have curve meeting curve

cases.name: 11-circle-inscribed
cases.note: B is tangent to all four of A's edges at once, from inside

cases.name: 12-vertex-on-arc
cases.note: B's corner rests on A's rim at 45 degrees, strictly inside one of A's quarter arcs rather than on a vertex of either

cases.name: 13-ellipse-arc-shared-swapped-partial
cases.note: B shares a 60-degree stretch of A's rotated ellipse but spells that rim with exchanged radii and a quarter-turned frame

cases.name: 14-tangent-external-mid-arcs
cases.note: equal circles touch externally at 45 degrees, in the interior of an arc on both paths

cases.name: 15-tangent-internal-mid-arcs
cases.note: the smaller circle touches A internally at 45 degrees, in the interior of an arc on both paths

cases.name: 16-four-vertices-on-edges
cases.note: every vertex of A lands in the interior of an edge of B, producing four simultaneous vertex-on-edge crossings

cases.name: 01-circle-in-circle
cases.note: B strictly inside A

cases.name: 02-circle-around-circle
cases.note: A strictly inside B (the reverse nesting order)

cases.name: 03-square-in-circle
cases.note: straight-edged island inside a curved boundary

cases.name: 04-circle-in-square
cases.note: curved island inside a straight boundary

cases.name: 05-circle-in-annulus-hole
cases.note: B sits in A's hole, touching nothing: two levels of nesting

cases.name: 06-circle-spanning-annulus
cases.note: B crosses both rings of the annulus

cases.name: 07-circle-in-bullseye-core
cases.note: B sits in A's innermost filled disc: three levels of nesting to walk through before reaching it

cases.name: 08-circle-in-bullseye-gap
cases.note: B sits in A's empty ring, so it is nested inside A and yet outside it

cases.name: 09-two-islands-in-circle
cases.note: both of B's components are contained, and neither contains the other

cases.name: 10-annulus-in-annulus-hole
cases.note: a hole inside a hole inside a hole: four levels of alternating containment

cases.name: 01-identical-circle
cases.note: every edge of A coincides with an edge of B

cases.name: 02-identical-square-reversed
cases.note: same boundary, opposite winding

cases.name: 03-identical-pentagram-evenodd
cases.note: coincident boundaries that are themselves self-intersecting

cases.name: 04-arc-vs-cubic-circle
cases.note: same nominal circle, two representations, ~2.7e-4 apart: near-coincident but not equal

cases.name: 05-offset-1e-9-square
cases.note: offset below EPS.point: edges should merge

cases.name: 06-offset-1e-12-circle
cases.note: offset at the edge of double precision for unit coordinates

cases.name: 07-identical-circle-rotated-start
cases.note: the same circle drawn from a different starting angle: the boundaries coincide but not one vertex of A meets a vertex of B

cases.name: 08-identical-annulus
cases.note: coincident on both rings at once, with the two winding oppositely

cases.name: 09-square-vs-subdivided-square
cases.note: the same square with twice as many vertices, so every coincident edge has a vertex of B in its interior

cases.name: 10-square-vs-degenerate-curves
cases.note: the same square drawn with a zero-length cubic, a collinear cubic and a collinear quadratic: identical geometry, no shared segment type

cases.name: 11-circle-vs-overlong-radii
cases.note: identical only if the SVG F.6.6 radius correction is applied; B's radii are half what its chords need

cases.name: 12-square-vs-zero-radius-arc
cases.note: identical only if a zero-radius arc is read as the straight line SVG F.6.2 says it is

cases.name: 13-ellipse-vs-swapped-radii
cases.note: the same rotated ellipse with rx/ry exchanged and phi advanced by 90 degrees

cases.name: 14-ellipse-vs-half-turn
cases.note: the same ellipse with its frame and starting point advanced by half a turn

cases.name: 15-circle-vs-negative-radius
cases.note: the same circle with a negative rx, which SVG normalizes to its absolute value

cases.name: 16-quadratic-vs-subdivided
cases.note: the same quadratic boundary with every segment split at t = 0.5

cases.name: 17-cubic-vs-subdivided
cases.note: the same cubic boundary with every segment split at t = 0.5

cases.name: 18-cubic-vs-reversed
cases.note: the same cubic boundary traversed in the opposite direction

cases.name: 01-square-and-circle
cases.note: separated shapes: intersection is empty, union has two components

cases.name: 02-annulus-and-square
cases.note: a hole-bearing component alongside a separate solid one

cases.name: 03-two-islands-and-bullseye
cases.note: two multi-component inputs, five components between them, no contact anywhere

cases.name: 04-island-between-islands
cases.note: B fits in the gap between A's two components: disjoint from both, and contained by neither

cases.name: 01-pentagram-x-circle-nonzero-nonzero
cases.note: self-intersecting A read as nonzero, B as nonzero

cases.name: 02-pentagram-x-circle-nonzero-evenodd
cases.note: self-intersecting A read as nonzero, B as evenodd

cases.name: 03-pentagram-x-circle-evenodd-nonzero
cases.note: self-intersecting A read as evenodd, B as nonzero

cases.name: 04-pentagram-x-circle-evenodd-evenodd
cases.note: self-intersecting A read as evenodd, B as evenodd

cases.name: 05-annulus-x-square-nonzero
cases.note: opposing-winding subpaths read as nonzero

cases.name: 06-annulus-x-square-evenodd
cases.note: opposing-winding subpaths read as evenodd

cases.name: 07-two-discs-x-square-nonzero
cases.note: two same-winding subpaths overlapping in a doubly-wound lens, read as nonzero: the lens is filled under non-zero and empty under even-odd

cases.name: 08-two-discs-x-square-evenodd
cases.note: two same-winding subpaths overlapping in a doubly-wound lens, read as evenodd: the lens is filled under non-zero and empty under even-odd

cases.name: 09-double-circle-x-square-nonzero
cases.note: a circle traversed twice round in one subpath, read as nonzero: the disc is filled under non-zero and wholly empty under even-odd

cases.name: 10-double-circle-x-square-evenodd
cases.note: a circle traversed twice round in one subpath, read as evenodd: the disc is filled under non-zero and wholly empty under even-odd

cases.name: 11-bowtie-x-circle-nonzero
cases.note: opposite-winding lobes meeting at a self-crossing, read as nonzero: both rules fill both lobes, so this pins that the rules agree where they should

cases.name: 12-bowtie-x-circle-evenodd
cases.note: opposite-winding lobes meeting at a self-crossing, read as evenodd: both rules fill both lobes, so this pins that the rules agree where they should

cases.name: 13-cancelled-circle-x-square-nonzero
cases.note: two coincident circles traversed in opposite directions cancel under nonzero, so A contributes no filled region

cases.name: 14-cancelled-circle-x-square-evenodd
cases.note: two coincident circles traversed in opposite directions cancel under evenodd, so A contributes no filled region

cases.name: 15-crossed-two-discs-nonzero
cases.note: two horizontal overlapping discs against two vertical ones, with both multiply-wound inputs read as nonzero

cases.name: 16-crossed-two-discs-evenodd
cases.note: two horizontal overlapping discs against two vertical ones, with both multiply-wound inputs read as evenodd

cases.name: 01-spike-vs-square
cases.note: zero-area spike protruding from an otherwise ordinary square

cases.name: 02-spike-through-boundary
cases.note: the spike is crossed by B's boundary

cases.name: 03-parallel-lines
cases.note: two wholly zero-area paths, not touching

cases.name: 04-crossing-lines
cases.note: two wholly zero-area paths crossing at the origin

cases.name: 05-degenerate-curves-x-circle
cases.note: a zero-length cubic, a collinear cubic and a collinear quadratic all cut by an ordinary curve

cases.name: 06-sliver-x-square
cases.note: a wedge under half a pixel thick crossing an ordinary edge: the area oracle can see the result, the raster oracle cannot

cases.name: 07-crossing-slivers
cases.note: two sub-pixel wedges crossing, so the intersection has an area of order 1e-6 and four vertices within 0.002 of each other

cases.name: 08-spike-along-edge
cases.note: the zero-area spike ends exactly on B's boundary, so the out-and-back pair terminates at a vertex it has to share

cases.name: 09-zero-length-line-in-square
cases.note: an ordinary square contains a repeated vertex and therefore an explicit zero-length line

cases.name: 10-point-subpath-and-square
cases.note: a point-only closed subpath sits alongside an ordinary filled component

cases.name: 11-quadratic-spike-x-square
cases.note: a quadratic is followed by its exact reverse and the retraced curve is crossed by B

cases.name: 12-cubic-spike-x-square
cases.note: a cubic is followed by its exact reverse and the retraced curve is crossed by B

cases.name: 01-large-arc-x-square
cases.note: every arc of A takes the long way round (largeArc set), which is the flag combination nothing else in the corpus uses

cases.name: 02-overlong-radii-x-square
cases.note: A's radii are half what its chords need, so the F.6.6 correction has to fire before anything else can be right

cases.name: 03-zero-radius-x-circle
cases.note: A's bottom edge is an arc of radius zero, which F.6.2 says to draw as a straight line

cases.name: 04-ellipse-x-ellipse-crossed
cases.note: two rotated ellipses at 70 degrees to each other: four transversal crossings, none of them on an axis of either

cases.name: 05-half-disc-x-half-disc
cases.note: each half-disc's chord crosses the other's arc, so all four crossings are curve-against-line and the two chords stay parallel

cases.name: 06-sweep-flags-x-square
cases.note: A's outer and inner arcs run with opposite sweep flags and both have largeArc set

cases.name: 07-same-endpoint-small-arc
cases.note: an arc whose endpoints coincide is omitted, with largeArc clear

cases.name: 08-same-endpoint-large-arc
cases.note: an arc whose endpoints coincide is still omitted when largeArc is set

cases.name: 01-gear-x-circle
cases.note: the circle cuts every one of the twelve teeth: 24 intersections spread over four arcs

cases.name: 02-gear-x-gear
cases.note: two gears offset by half a tooth, so the teeth interlock and every one of them crosses two of the other's edges

cases.name: 03-comb-x-comb
cases.note: two combs at right angles: the teeth of each cross the teeth of the other in a grid

cases.name: 04-gear-x-annulus
cases.note: both rings of the annulus cut the teeth, so the result is a ring of alternating faces

cases.name: 05-gear-tangent-circle
cases.note: the circle contains the gear and touches all twelve tooth tips at once

cases.name: 06-bowtie-x-bowtie
cases.note: two self-crossing polygons share their central crossing, creating an eight-way vertex

cases.name: 07-pentagram-x-pentagram
cases.note: two self-intersecting stars interleave at half a point step

cases.name: 08-loop-cubic-x-loop-cubic
cases.note: two self-crossing cubic loops collide with their singular structure centred together

cases.name: 09-annulus-x-annulus
cases.note: both inner and outer rings of two offset annuli cross, producing nested alternating faces

cases.name: 10-bullseye-x-annulus
cases.note: five nested rings across two inputs intersect away from their symmetry axes

cases.name: 11-two-islands-x-two-islands
cases.note: horizontal and vertical pairs of disconnected components overlap in four separate regions
